paragraphs: While Kenna was happily hugging him, Kent dove into her profile.
Just like Calix, her race changed from Void Beast to Soul Demon. However, unlike how Calix only became a Soul Demon, there was a slight change to Kenna’s race.
It turned to [Soul Void Demon].
This gave her both the qualities of a Void Beast and a Soul Demon.
She also came with a Reaper class. However, while she can operate on the soul level, her greatest strength will show itself when void battles are put into focus.
It leans more toward void manipulation on the soul level.

Job Class: [Void Reaper] ↠ Description: With untamed control over the void, the soul warrior can harness the overwhelming power of the void to her advantage. The deeper her understanding of the void, the stronger her control.
The description did justice to most of what Kent needed to know. However, with how much he knew when it came to the Void, there were many avenues to consider.
From the little he learned from Axiom, there are variations of the void. There are the physical, astral, and mental versions of the void.

The physical aspect involved using the void as a medium to move much faster in the physical plane. That happened to be Axiom’s field, so he gave a good explanation, which helped Kent understand quite a lot.
Thanks to that knowledge, he knew Kenna’s version was not the physical aspect of the void.
This means she is on the Astral Void path.
And if that is the case, then she can be considered the perfect assassin. If she can command Astral Void essence, then no soul will be safe from her reach.
While it is hard to hurt the soul, considering soul attacks are a two-way street. If a soul attack backfires, it returns to the attacker, making them experience what they intended for their opponent.
But once they reach a certain level, one can easily defeat their opponent with soul attacks.
However, over the years, soul items had been repurposed into soul defense artefacts. Most of these items can even take on an attack from a god.
In fact, during the Era of the Soul Sentinel, she had crafted many soul items that could take on even a soul attack from a Supreme.
So if someone like Calix were to meet someone with such an item, he would lose, and there is nothing anyone can do about it—unless they have a Kenna.

Kenna’s void power had to do with the soul, so against someone who has a soul defense item, she can use the void to bypass it, or even if she cannot bypass it and attack directly, she can deal powerful damage to the item.
That makes her the perfect battle partner Calix could ask for. She will open a path for him to attack. So regardless of the opponent she meets, with enough control, she can kill them.
Kent moved ahead to the Affinity section.
Affinities: [Void Affinity] and [Soul Affinity]
The [Void Affinity] had to do with her control over the void, while her [Soul Affinity] tackled the soul. While she had only two affinities, compared to Calix’s three, they were perfect for her.
The [Soul Affinity] will come into play when she manages to bypass the defense of a soul.
As for her Aspects, she came with three powerful ones.
Aspects: [Astral Severance], [Void Infiltrator], and [Reaper’s Silence]
[Astral Severance]: Has the ability to see and sever connections within the soul. As long as she can see these connections, she can sever them.
"Hmm, that is a bit over the top, don’t you think?" Kent said, turning to look at Kenna, who was cuddled in his arms. "Your Astral Severance Aspect is a bit overpowered."
"I know, right. It is so cool." Kenna smiled happily.
"Way cooler than Calix’s," Kent decided to make her even happier, since she seemed to be in the mood already.
"Care to throw more light on it?"

"Sure. With the Astral Severance Aspect, I can see all connections in the soul and sever them completely. This means I can sever connections such as soul bonds, contracts, regeneration threads, artifact bindings, and others.
So if my opponent has a soul weapon, the moment I see that soul thread, cutting their connection to their weapon is as simple as swinging my dagger.
Soul contracts to beasts, slaves, and many others can be severed. Anything with a connection to her soul can be severed easily."
"So if I were to meet a beast tamer, with you around, the moment you find the threads binding his tamed beasts to him and sever them, he would lose all connection to them."
"Yes. Once cut, there will be no way to reattach them again."
"Damn. That is awesome." Kent was clearly impressed.
"What about the other two?"
"The [Void Infiltrator] Aspect allows me to infiltrate the soul through the void, while the [Reaper’s Silence] Aspect makes it so my infiltration is as silent as possible."
"So in other words, you can enter my soul without me knowing."
"Yes. However, I will never enter Master’s soul if he doesn’t want me to," Kenna said with a cute pout.
"Tch, as if you haven’t already tried."
Kenna blushed. "I just wanted to see if my abilities work. Safe to say they work, and I also had the scare of my life when I infiltrated your soul. Also, how did you know I infiltrated your soul?"
"I didn’t at first. However, when you saw the [Underworld Soul River], you became scared and lost focus, which caused your aura to leak. That was how I learned it was you."

"That gate of yours is scary, Master. I would never enter your soul sea again. Also, it wasn’t like I could hurt you. You are my Master, and it seems you have the Seal of the Soul Dao, so unless I reach Tier 30, I can’t break past that seal.
By the way, who gave you that seal? If I can become friends with them, we can collaborate and create powerful soul attacks."
"I will introduce you later. But first, how about you tell me your Innate Abilities?"
She has two passive Innate Abilities and one active Innate Ability. The passive ones are [Void Phase Instinct] and [Astral Marking].
The [Void Phase Instinct] allows her to always be within the Astral Plane and the Void Plane. In that state, physical attacks won’t work on her.
For the [Astral Marking], she can instinctively mark a soul once she senses it. The mark reveals connection points between the soul and the artifact. This allows her to know exactly where to sever.
As for the active Innate Ability, [Void Corrosion], it allows her to use her void energy to corrode soul constructs.

This means that even if she can’t sever a soul thread, just by leaving her mark, she can use her void energy to corrode things like soul shields, soul puppets, defensive soul arrays, binding contracts, divine soul chains, and more.
Basically, she has the means to weaken the soul, making it easy for her to destroy it. It is the best possible combination a person can have.
"You are perfect, Kenna. We are going to have so much fun together."
Kenna nodded. She pulled back and opened her palm, and seven triangular-shaped crystals appeared.

"These are the soul crystals I formed. Since you can’t expand your soul yet, you can use them to expand the soul universe or give them to the people linked to your soul. I can see that the stronger they grow, the stronger you also become."

However, with how much he knew when it came to the Void, there were many avenues to consider.
From the little he learned from Axiom, there are variations of the void.
There are the physical, astral, and mental versions of the void.
The physical aspect involved using the void as a medium to move much faster in the physical plane.
That happened to be Axiom’s field, so he gave a good explanation, which helped Kent understand quite a lot.
Thanks to that knowledge, he knew Kenna’s version was not the physical aspect of the void.
This means she is on the Astral Void path.
And if that is the case, then she can be considered the perfect assassin.
If she can command Astral Void essence, then no soul will be safe from her reach.
While it is hard to hurt the soul, considering soul attacks are a two-way street.
If a soul attack backfires, it returns to the attacker, making them experience what they intended for their opponent.
But once they reach a certain level, one can easily defeat their opponent with soul attacks.
However, over the years, soul items had been repurposed into soul defense artefacts.
Most of these items can even take on an attack from a god.
In fact, during the Era of the Soul Sentinel, she had crafted many soul items that could take on even a soul attack from a Supreme.
So if someone like Calix were to meet someone with such an item, he would lose, and there is nothing anyone can do about it—unless they have a Kenna.

Kenna’s void power had to do with the soul, so against someone who has a soul defense item, she can use the void to bypass it, or even if she cannot bypass it and attack directly, she can deal powerful damage to the item.
That makes her the perfect battle partner Calix could ask for.
She will open a path for him to attack.
So regardless of the opponent she meets, with enough control, she can kill them.
Kent moved ahead to the Affinity section.
Affinities: [Void Affinity] and [Soul Affinity]
The [Void Affinity] had to do with her control over the void, while her [Soul Affinity] tackled the soul.
While she had only two affinities, compared to Calix’s three, they were perfect for her.
The [Soul Affinity] will come into play when she manages to bypass the defense of a soul.
As for her Aspects, she came with three powerful ones.
Aspects: [Astral Severance], [Void Infiltrator], and [Reaper’s Silence]
[Astral Severance]: Has the ability to see and sever connections within the soul.
As long as she can see these connections, she can sever them.
"Hmm, that is a bit over the top, don’t you think?" Kent said, turning to look at Kenna, who was cuddled in his arms.
"Your Astral Severance Aspect is a bit overpowered."
"I know, right.
It is so cool." Kenna smiled happily.
"Way cooler than Calix’s," Kent decided to make her even happier, since she seemed to be in the mood already.
"Care to throw more light on it?"
"Sure.
With the Astral Severance Aspect, I can see all connections in the soul and sever them completely.
This means I can sever connections such as soul bonds, contracts, regeneration threads, artifact bindings, and others.
So if my opponent has a soul weapon, the moment I see that soul thread, cutting their connection to their weapon is as simple as swinging my dagger.
Soul contracts to beasts, slaves, and many others can be severed.
Anything with a connection to her soul can be severed easily."
"So if I were to meet a beast tamer, with you around, the moment you find the threads binding his tamed beasts to him and sever them, he would lose all connection to them."
"Yes.
Once cut, there will be no way to reattach them again."
"Damn.
That is awesome." Kent was clearly impressed.
"What about the other two?"
"The [Void Infiltrator] Aspect allows me to infiltrate the soul through the void, while the [Reaper’s Silence] Aspect makes it so my infiltration is as silent as possible."
"So in other words, you can enter my soul without me knowing."
"Yes.
However, I will never enter Master’s soul if he doesn’t want me to," Kenna said with a cute pout.
"Tch, as if you haven’t already tried."
Kenna blushed.
"I just wanted to see if my abilities work.
Safe to say they work, and I also had the scare of my life when I infiltrated your soul.
Also, how did you know I infiltrated your soul?"
"I didn’t at first.
However, when you saw the [Underworld Soul River], you became scared and lost focus, which caused your aura to leak.
That was how I learned it was you."
"That gate of yours is scary, Master.
I would never enter your soul sea again.
Also, it wasn’t like I could hurt you.
You are my Master, and it seems you have the Seal of the Soul Dao, so unless I reach Tier 30, I can’t break past that seal.
By the way, who gave you that seal?
If I can become friends with them, we can collaborate and create powerful soul attacks."
"I will introduce you later.
But first, how about you tell me your Innate Abilities?"
She has two passive Innate Abilities and one active Innate Ability.
The passive ones are [Void Phase Instinct] and [Astral Marking].
The [Void Phase Instinct] allows her to always be within the Astral Plane and the Void Plane.
In that state, physical attacks won’t work on her.
For the [Astral Marking], she can instinctively mark a soul once she senses it.
The mark reveals connection points between the soul and the artifact.
This allows her to know exactly where to sever.
As for the active Innate Ability, [Void Corrosion], it allows her to use her void energy to corrode soul constructs.

This means that even if she can’t sever a soul thread, just by leaving her mark, she can use her void energy to corrode things like soul shields, soul puppets, defensive soul arrays, binding contracts, divine soul chains, and more.
Basically, she has the means to weaken the soul, making it easy for her to destroy it.
It is the best possible combination a person can have.
"You are perfect, Kenna.
We are going to have so much fun together."
Kenna nodded.
She pulled back and opened her palm, and seven triangular-shaped crystals appeared.
"These are the soul crystals I formed.
Since you can’t expand your soul yet, you can use them to expand the soul universe or give them to the people linked to your soul.
I can see that the stronger they grow, the stronger you also become."

chapters.title: Chapter 1431: Soul Crystals
paragraphs: Kent received the Soul Crystals from Kenna.
He could sense the strongest and purest form of soul essence condensed in each crystal. This made him understand why he could advance from Tier 16 to Tier 19 when he created Calix.
So far, aside from using them to increase his soul cultivation, he now knew he could use them to expand, decorate, and strengthen his Soul Universe.
But there is more...
"Are those the only uses for it?" he asked.
"No. I used two to create the waterfall and the darkness domain."
"Oh, so you also can do that, huh?"
"Yeah. To use it, you just have to imagine what you want and activate the crystal by channelling your energy into it."

Kent left his brow furrowed a bit, blown away by how easy and ridiculous it was to use the Soul Crystal. He expected it to be technical, since Calix made it sound like he needed special knowledge to use it.
But hearing how easy it was to use it, he was blown away.
Merely imagining the thing he wanted to create and activating the Soul Crystal was as simple as it could get.
Of course, he knew there was more to it, but for now, he only needed to know this much.

If the process was this simple on the surface, then regardless of how deep he went, there wouldn’t be much to consider, since at the end of the day, he could create whatever he wanted by merely thinking about it.
He already had knowledge of conceptualisation. The Death Star Cannon came about from what he was able to imagine.
If he was able to conceptualise something that grand, then, when it came to creating basic stuff like a weapon or artefacts, he could easily handle it.
One good thing about the Soul Crystal is that its use is instant. The moment the idea was formed, the crystal would form it. It was that simple and fast.
Even better, if he were to master conceptualisation now, when he becomes a god, where all battles are fought through conceptualisation of the laws, he could easily handle it.
So with these Soul Crystals and the Soul Universe in general, if he planned well, he could easily get things done.
"This is awesome to know. I guess I will hold on to them for now."
"You do that. I, on the other hand, have plans to form more since I can see you have added more Immortal-grade Soul Spirits to the fold."
Kent nodded, already pleased to hear that. The more soul crystals, the better.
Kenna was a Core Immortal with two Immortal Qi. Although already powerful enough, if she were to become a True Immortal, things would be even better.
"So what are your next plans aside from wanting to form more Soul Crystals?"
"I want to form Immortal Qi. I only have two, which is too embarrassing for a Core Immortal. So I want to form at least three more.

Thankfully, I have all the resources I need in one place, so I will be spending the next couple of months working on that. I am sure Calix and that weird guy would be doing their own thing to grow stronger, so I must hurry."
"Which weird guy?" Kent asked. He knew she was referring to the third soul warrior.
So far, he had created three Soul Warriors.

The first was Calix, whom he formed from the soul of a demon. The second was Kenna, who seemed to like it when she hugged him. And the third was the Temple Master, who was killed on the last level of the Void Temple.
He was the Void Beast whom Axiom and his pals had kidnapped and tortured when they hijacked the Void Temple.
Kent actually felt pity for him, so he let him off easily. In the end, he came back as a Soul Warrior candidate, so he decided to add him to the Soul Legion.
"That guy only does one thing. He sits in a meditative posture facing a weird-looking mural all day. I tried to talk to him, but he ignored me, so I stopped going to him. Very weird guy."
Kent smiled, already eager to meet his third Soul Warrior. He should like a whole mood.
However, with his soul still healing, he decided to get that handled first. After all, he had time on his hands even while inside the Soul Universe.
From what he had seen so far, it was clear to him that if he played his cards well, he would be walking away after his next mission with so much power.
After all, the stronger Soul Spirits he adds to his stockpile, the stronger his Soul Warriors will become. And the stronger they become, the more he benefits.
For now, he would take things one step at a time.
He would be heading to a Unique Planet soon, so he needed all the strength he could get. Once that was handled, he would think of what to do next.
He asked Kenna a couple more times. Once that was handled, he submerged his entire body into the pool to heal much faster.
[Planet Kenai - 9th Floor of the Planet Killer Dungeon]
Meanwhile, somewhere on Planet Kenai, Axiom, Kailan, and Kol stood behind a tall mountain, evil grins on their faces.
They are lying in wait for the Immortal Monarch heading their way.
Axiom is a Void Architect.
His strongest ability is strategy and crafting. When he appeared on the 9th floor alone, he didn’t panic or even bother reaching out to anyone.
He tapped into the void, which, thanks to his Immortal Monarch strength and the fact that he has 9 Immortal Qi, enabled him to see more than anyone.
Initially, something prevented him from sensing the 7 Calamity Beasts. However, his surveillance revealed that there were many powerful beings on the planet.
So, as an architect, he began crafting void mechanisms to withstand whatever dangers would come their way.
A few seconds ago, one was triggered.
Knowing someone was heading toward them, he pulled his friends away and waited for them to walk into his trap.
"Nice catch, Axiom. I knew you would always find a way for us to have some fun," Kol said, spinning a thick arrow between his fingers.
"True. Standing around and doing nothing is boring. It is like being back inside the Void Temple all over again," Kailan also spoke, leaning on the blunt end of his spear.
Axiom smiled and replied, "I know. So now that we have found a prey, I say we make sure it regrets ever thinking it had cornered us."
Kol and Kailan nodded.
Kailan is an Immortal King with 8 Immortal Qi, while Kol is a True Immortal with 7 Immortal Qi. Just Kol alone would be enough to handle the Immortal Monarch coming after Vexthra and her team.
However, because they were bored, they wanted to team up on him and have some fun.
Seated in a lotus posture not far from Unity’s cocoon, Vexthra smirked and chose not to interfere in their business.
Kent had already told her not to worry about Axiom and his pals. They are destructive and hate following orders, so letting them have fun occasionally isn’t too bad.
As for the Immortal Monarch coming toward Vexthra’s team, just when he came out of the void and was able to move forward, Axiom appeared, and his body froze.
"Greetings. The name is Axiom. I will be your friend for the next couple of hours if you don’t mind."
Axiom snapped his fingers, and reality shifted.
The next second, the Immortal Monarch found himself standing inside the void, surrounded in a triangular formation by three evil-looking immortals.

chapters.title: Chapter 1432: Black Beard method
paragraphs: During the Primordial Era, when Chaos crazily ventured into the Void Realm, he met and rescued 69 Void Beasts who were considered criminals of their race.
They aided him in his conquest of the Void Realm, and when he was leaving, they followed him.

Later, when the Void Beasts invaded this universe, they stood and fought for him till every last one of them died. They believed in him, and so they gave their all, and thanks to them, this universe still stood.
Several years later, Axiom, Kailan, and Kol, three of the 69, found their way back to their master.
However, by coming to this universe, they felt restricted. They aren’t having as much fun as they did back in their universe. So they always started looking for ways to get entertained.
On the other hand, Keir was once a brave warrior who led many warriors into harrowing battles. He survived many wars and earned a good name for himself. His reputation was unprecedented.
However, behind that perfect persona was a psychopath who loved to prey on the weak and vulnerable ladies.
He had killed and done all kinds of disgusting things to them to the point that when he was finally caught, many lost their belief in what is considered righteous.
The great warrior they all believed in turned out to be a scum of society.
He was rotten to the core, and so he was sent to Planet Kenai, which, to the rest of the universe, is called the Pitt. It is a place where only suffering and pain can be found.
However, while he may be evil, he was also a good warrior, so he adapted, and for thousands of years, he had gathered strength through slaughter and all kinds of despicable means.
He never expected that just when he found a new pool of prey to take advantage of, he would find himself surrounded by three people that, from a mere glance, he knew were even more evil than he was.

Axiom, Kailan, and Kol are Void Beasts, so of course, they are as evil as they come. They had done all kinds of despicable things before they met Chaos. It was through their deeds that all 69 of them were captured and imprisoned.
To be imprisoned in the void realm might mean that, at heart, they are even more evil than the Void Beasts that attacked the universe during the Primordial Era.
Keir knew he was fucked beyond comprehension.
"Looks like he is scared," Kol said, his bow held firm in his grip.
Axiom created a battleground inside the void, so while they found themselves in there, their surroundings were a burnt forest, one where the smell of danger could be sensed.
"Of course, he is scared. I can tell he is a warrior like us, so there is just no way he couldn’t tell we are a danger to his life," Axiom grinned, his expression filled with satisfaction.
Toying with his prey is something he had mastered a very long time ago. As a Void Architect, he can create all kinds of mechanisms that, once a prey falls into them, their fate is sealed.
Keir had fallen into his trap, and so he wanted to take his dear time and enjoy torturing him.

"I suggest we use the Black Beard method. It is the perfect torture for him," Kailan said, already eager to try it. "It is evil, painful, and stimulating. I would very much have the time of my life if we use that."
Axiom turned toward Kol as if to ask for his opinion. "I have no problem with that. As long as he screams, I would be happy."
"Then it is decided, we will use the Black Beard method."
"Great. Now, let’s talk weapons. I suggest we use Void Daggers laced with Pain Stimulant Poison. This way, every cut will increase the pain severalfold."
Kol shook his head. "Daggers are good, but I will use Void Needles."
Axiom nodded. "That can be arranged, but I am with Kailan. We will use Void Daggers while you use the needles."
"I am okay with that arrangement also."

"Then fine. I will use needles, and you guys can use daggers," Kol grinned, turning to face Keir, who was frozen in place, his expression pale. Looking at him tremble, his void heart trembled with delight.
"Let’s talk segments. Since I will be using needles, I think I should take the head while you two share from his neck downwards. You can have him by dividing him vertically into two."
"That is perfect. I will take the left half, and Kailan will take the right."

Once everything had been planned to the last detail, Axiom turned to Keir. "It is your bad luck that you met us in this life. We are the kind of people who lack basic emotions, so what we find funny may be painful to you.

Regardless, when all things are considered, you aren’t a good person either. So I will advise you not to hold a grudge in your next life. Who knows, maybe we are the reality check you needed before you die."
Keir trembled even more. His legs gave out, and he dropped to his knees. He was about to open his mouth to plead, but Axiom moved his finger up and down, and his lips were stitched tight.
"I hate it when they plead. It makes it seem like I am doing something bad."
"Indeed. From where I stand, we are merely doing what many cannot or wouldn’t dare do."
"You should thank us. Not many can boast and say they died at the hands of void beasts after the primordial era."
"Yes. This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, so cherish it."
Tears rolled down Keir’s face. He had done all kinds of evil things, but he had never met people who discussed evil as if it were a good thing.
Axiom and his pals had surpassed his expectations, and that scared him. And with his lips sealed, he had no choice but to let his tears speak for him.
However, seeing the tears fall down his face, the three Void Beasts felt their hearts swell with happiness.
"He is ready, boys. Let’s scar his soul so that in his next life, he will walk the path of righteousness. As the master used to say, when they do evil, punish them with evil."
Axiom waved his hand, and ropes with hooks latched onto Keir’s hands and feet and lifted him into the air. His hands and legs were pierced, making him hang loose in the air.
"Let’s start from 2 km and increase it by 1km every three attacks."
They moved back 2 km, and each retrieved their weapons. Axiom and Kailan drew daggers, while Kol retrieved needles.
Kailan was first to attack. He threw the dagger, which zipped through the air with deadly precision and passed by Keir’s neck, leaving a thin cut.
Keir moaned his pain, more tears falling from his eyes. It was a simple cut, but the pain that came with it was just too much for him to handle.
Axiom attacked next, leaving another cut on his neck. The same reaction came from Keir, who was being stimulated by a special void-rich poison laced on the daggers.
"My turn," Kol grinned and flicked his finger, sending out a small needle directly at Keir’s eye. It stabbed through and came out from the back of his head.
He screamed, which came out as a moan. This made the three of them grin. What followed next were several throws, each leaving a cut or tiny holes.
Six hours later, after millions of throws and cuts, Keir couldn’t take it anymore and died. It was only then that the three Void Beasts stopped.
"That was awesome. We should find more."
Kol’s advice was accepted, and so for the duration of the time Unity would be spending in the cocoon, the three Void Beasts would roam the entire planet, killing one criminal after another.

I will use needles, and you guys can use daggers," Kol grinned, turning to face Keir, who was frozen in place, his expression pale.
Looking at him tremble, his void heart trembled with delight.
"Let’s talk segments.
Since I will be using needles, I think I should take the head while you two share from his neck downwards.
You can have him by dividing him vertically into two."
"That is perfect.
I will take the left half, and Kailan will take the right."
Once everything had been planned to the last detail, Axiom turned to Keir.
"It is your bad luck that you met us in this life.
We are the kind of people who lack basic emotions, so what we find funny may be painful to you.
Regardless, when all things are considered, you aren’t a good person either.
So I will advise you not to hold a grudge in your next life.
Who knows, maybe we are the reality check you needed before you die."
Keir trembled even more.
His legs gave out, and he dropped to his knees.
He was about to open his mouth to plead, but Axiom moved his finger up and down, and his lips were stitched tight.
"I hate it when they plead.
It makes it seem like I am doing something bad."
"Indeed.
From where I stand, we are merely doing what many cannot or wouldn’t dare do."
"You should thank us.
Not many can boast and say they died at the hands of void beasts after the primordial era."
"Yes.
This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, so cherish it."
Tears rolled down Keir’s face.
He had done all kinds of evil things, but he had never met people who discussed evil as if it were a good thing.
Axiom and his pals had surpassed his expectations, and that scared him.
And with his lips sealed, he had no choice but to let his tears speak for him.
However, seeing the tears fall down his face, the three Void Beasts felt their hearts swell with happiness.
"He is ready, boys.
Let’s scar his soul so that in his next life, he will walk the path of righteousness.
As the master used to say, when they do evil, punish them with evil."
Axiom waved his hand, and ropes with hooks latched onto Keir’s hands and feet and lifted him into the air.
His hands and legs were pierced, making him hang loose in the air.
"Let’s start from 2 km and increase it by 1km every three attacks."
They moved back 2 km, and each retrieved their weapons.
Axiom and Kailan drew daggers, while Kol retrieved needles.
Kailan was first to attack.
He threw the dagger, which zipped through the air with deadly precision and passed by Keir’s neck, leaving a thin cut.
Keir moaned his pain, more tears falling from his eyes.
It was a simple cut, but the pain that came with it was just too much for him to handle.
Axiom attacked next, leaving another cut on his neck.
The same reaction came from Keir, who was being stimulated by a special void-rich poison laced on the daggers.
"My turn," Kol grinned and flicked his finger, sending out a small needle directly at Keir’s eye.
It stabbed through and came out from the back of his head.
He screamed, which came out as a moan.
This made the three of them grin.
What followed next were several throws, each leaving a cut or tiny holes.
Six hours later, after millions of throws and cuts, Keir couldn’t take it anymore and died.
It was only then that the three Void Beasts stopped.
"That was awesome.
We should find more."
Kol’s advice was accepted, and so for the duration of the time Unity would be spending in the cocoon, the three Void Beasts would roam the entire planet, killing one criminal after another.

chapters.title: Chapter 1433: Strange Painting
paragraphs: Kent spent 8 days inside the pool before he came out.
By the time he came out, his soul had healed and even become stronger than before.
"This pool is a treasure."

Kenna nodded. "The water flowing down is filled with purified soul essence, so naturally, it has all the qualities to heal and strengthen the soul. As the soul universe grows stronger, so will this pool."
"Then I will frequent here, since I know for a fact I will be sustaining more soul damage soon." Kent laughed. He plans to use the Underworld Soul River again, so that is an automatic soul injury.
"The master is always welcome in my domain."
Kent walked out of the pool, Kenna still in his arms. She seemed a bit more clingy than she was supposed to be, but Kent didn’t mind.
Clingy is nice.
After all, when he enters the star gateway, he won’t be able to talk to his wives until he is out. But with Kenna around, he would have someone to hold and cuddle with.

Kenna had no plans to sleep with him, which is nice. Kent also had no plans to take such a step—not that he wouldn’t if Kenna offered. But since she seems to like it just by being with him and close to him, he wouldn’t mind ending things where they are now.
He quickly put on his clothes and got ready to leave.
"I will be in seclusion for a while, but if you need me, I will be there."
Kent nodded and soon left the waterfall. This time, he didn’t spend minutes walking through the darkness. Kenna sent him away with a snap of her finger.
Once he was out, he quickly made his way toward the third soul warrior’s residence. In less than five minutes, he arrived before a small mountain made from what appeared to be a stone-glass hybrid.

There is no concrete name for it, since it has the look of both glass and stone. He flew over, and soon, he saw someone sitting in a quiet posture, staring at a mural that had a painting of a bow on it.
"Looks like Kenna wasn’t joking. All he really does is stare at a painting all day," Kent muttered, looking at the back of the figure seated in a lotus posture.
He noticed he had become a True Immortal instead of his Core Immortal strength. That was a big leap for him, which in a way added to his own strength.

But aside from that, as Kent began to focus more on the mural, he couldn’t help but feel some of the ancient power emanating from it. The longer he stared at it, the more he started to see that the mural was not as simple as it looked.

Even more insidious, the longer he stared at it, the more he couldn’t help but feel like it was calling out to him. It is weird that a painting would be calling out to him when he had never held a bow before.
But this feeling sparked his curiosity.
"Tower, what is this mural? More importantly, can you identify the bow in the painting?" he asked his only trusted source.
[I am not sure, but it looks like the Bow of Calamity.]
"Bow of Calamity. What is that?"
[The Bow of Calamity was the weapon wielded by the Calamity King. He led the battle against the Calamity Beasts, where he fought and died like the honourable warrior he was.
Legend has it he was the greatest archer to ever live in the history of the Universe.
From what has been recorded, when he fell, his bow fought on its own, dealing the last strike that the Calamity King couldn’t before he died.
After the war, it vanished, and nobody had ever seen it again.]
"I see. Sounds like it was a legendary weapon."

[It was. However, I am not sure whether this painting is the Bow of Calamity or not. What I can say, however, is that this mural is no simple painting. There is something mystical about that even I can’t figure it out.]
Kent nodded and decided to move closer. Just as he moved, he sensed the air around him twist and turn. The next second, he was standing before the mural.
"Hmm, Space Law, I suppose," Kent muttered, a bit stunned and a bit happy to see what his third soul warrior could do.
"Space Law. I have just comprehended it from the mural and have been waiting for you to come so I could test it on you."
"Looks like you have mastered it. Congratulations. Space Displacement is a difficult law aspect to comprehend."
"Oh, does the master also understand Space Law?"
Kent smiled and shook his head. "Unfortunately, no. However, I used to know someone who had mastered this aspect of the universal laws."
Inaya, the Sword Immortal that Jest met in the Whispering Wind Sword Sect, came to mind.
Although he couldn’t shake off the feeling that she and he are a bad pair—considering whenever he thinks of her, his body shudders—she was someone he knew had mastered the Space Law to some degree.
He himself had taken the path of the Void when he reached the Sword Legend stage. However, Inaya was someone who had walked the path of Space Law.
That was how he knew the space law his third soul warrior used was space displacement. Jest had learned alot about her just in case she came after her.

"It is all in the past now," he turned and looked at the mural. "Though I have to ask, how were you able to comprehend Space Law from merely staring at a painting? Also, where did this painting come from?"
"It was already here when I arrived. As for how I was able to learn Space Law from it, I didn’t. The painting taught me on its own."
"Huh?"
"Yeah. It’s shocking, but that was what happened. After you killed me, I entered a dark place. However, after a while, I returned as a different person. When I opened my eyes, this thing was here.

It called out to me and offered to teach me the Space Law if I wanted to learn. Of course, I accepted. After all, I already have a deep understanding of the Void Law, so adding Space Law seemed like the best option.
By the way, you can call me Bello."

Kent nodded, but he was in shock. All Bello had just said sounded too good to be true. However, if he were to think of all that had happened in this short time he spent inside the Soul Universe and those that happened in the past, he couldn’t help but wonder if something else is at play here.
In fact, the entire nature of the Soul Universe is weird. There is just no way he is following the rules of the universe when inside his Soul Universe.

Creating weapons, in a way, is normal. However, when he moved ahead to creating literal warriors, that is where he crossed the line. However, even if he had crossed the line, the heavens didn’t seem to care.
He didn’t put much thought into it before, but now, he can’t help but wonder what is at play here.
"Oh, I found this scroll before the painting. I couldn’t open it, so I figured it was for you." Bello handed a scroll to Kent, who, the moment he touched it, felt like it was meant for him.
He closed his eyes for a moment, then he opened them. Under Bello’s gaze, the scroll unfurled.
Kent read the first line, which, even before he could finish it, made a smile appear on his face.
"Sup dude, it is your big brother Paragon writing."

chapters.title: Chapter 1434: Paragon’s Overpowered Gift
paragraphs: "Sup dude, it is your big brother Paragon writing."
"I knew it," Kent smirked.
Bello gave him a curious look but said nothing. He knew the scroll contained something important to Kent, considering that with a mere glance, he came to such a conclusion.
He knew the person who wrote the scroll.
Kent had his suspicions, but he didn’t dare voice them.
The stronger the Soul Universe became, the more his suspicion grew that Paragon was pulling strings behind the scenes.
After all, he was the one who gave the Soul Universe to him, so it was only right that it had such an overpowered nature.
The Paragon is like the outlier of the rules.
Kent himself knew sometimes, he didn’t play by the rules. However, unlike the Paragon, he is bound by the rules to some extent. He can’t go wield like Paragon.
Also, instead of hating him, the heavens actually like him.
However, when it comes to the Paragon, the heavens hate him, and as such, he always does things that will piss them off. The Soul Universe is one of such things.
However, because the heavens love him, they didn’t see it as a slap in their face. If anything, they are happy Kent has something this powerful.
In the grand scheme of things, it will aid him in what is coming.
The only thing was, while the Soul Universe is already overpowered, Paragon keeps pulling strings in the background, making it even more overpowered.
One of such strings was what he was about to read.

"I know you keep wondering just how someone can be both handsome, intelligent, and overpowered at the same time. In my defense, I never asked for any of it, but since we are here now, I can only say that when it comes to making things that don’t make sense, I excel.
My first job and reason for living is to piss the heavens off. They hate me, but they love you. So I decided to make things easy for you by giving you an edge.
That was why I decided to include this mural among many others inside the Soul Universe. I always believe that when the right tools are given to the right person, they make good use of them.
On that note, I hereby introduce the Mural of Calamity. It is the only painting of the Calamity Dao that I met a very long time ago during my exploration of an unfriendly universe.

Let me tell you, that trip nearly cost me my life and the life of a friend of mine. He is blind, by the way, but he can see better than anyone. One dangerous bastard who just doesn’t know when to stop.

When we met the Calamity Dao, we had a nice conversation that lasted 200 years. When we finally managed to escape thanks to another friend of mine, I decided to paint this to house the inheritance of Calamity.
I had no use for it because I am a Paragon, and my two pals had their own inheritances, so I decided to send it to you.

I know you are a True Primordial, which means you already have a Dao. But since you happen to have some relationship with your universe, I suppose bestowing it on one of your subordinates will be fine.
If they can bypass the restrictions on it and come face-to-face with Calamity, I can guarantee they will become a valuable asset to you.
Of course, there is a good chance they will die, so pick the right one. Also, Calamity is in a way related to you, so be sure to send him my regards when you meet one day.
That will be all. Good luck, and be sure to make good use of this mural. Who knows, we will meet again soon enough.
Oh, say hi to my pal Kaizo for me. Tell him we will pick up where we left off the last time."
Kent continued to stare at the contents of the scroll for a few minutes before a sigh escaped his lips.
"Too much to process right now." He turned and looked at the mural for a few more minutes before he turned to Bello.
"I have some good and bad news for you. Which one do you want to hear first?"
"Good news."

"Okay. The good news is that this mural contains the inheritance of the Calamity Dao. Whoever can inherit it will become a legendary warrior. However, the bad news is that there is a chance you would die before inheriting it."
"Oh, that explains the strange door I saw inside the painting."
"What door?"

"There is a door standing at the center of the space where I comprehended the Space Law. It has seven locks on it, which, now that I know what is contained within the painting, I believe are seals that must be broken to access the inheritance."
"I suppose you have a point. However, until we know what those locks are, we cannot risk it."
Bello thought for a moment, then asked, "Does that mean I can’t use it to improve my understanding of the Space Law?"

"You can use it. However, don’t touch the locks for the time being. I will do some more research and see what I can find. Once I manage to establish a good understanding, we will see where to go next."
"Okay, Master."
Kent nodded.
Although the Mural of Calamity sounded like a priceless treasure, there is just no way he would mess around with it. Paragon warned him of how dangerous Calamity was, so he would be cautious.
He also hinted that he has some connection to the Calamity Dao. This information brought his mind back to what the Tower said when he asked about the painting of the bow.
According to her, the bow resembles the bow wielded by the Calamity King. If Paragon said he had some connection to Calamity, could it be that he was the Calamity King?
Kent suspected as much. After all, he has already uncovered memories of legendary lives he had lived, and he is aware he has lived 13 such lives, so there must be some connection here.
He knew Chaos lived during the Primordial Era, where he fought the Void Beasts.
Jest/Lord Genesis lived during the Divine Era and fought the Foreign Race.
Faceless Assassin lived during the Shadow Era and fought the Shadow creatures/fiends.
Ruthless Bandit lived during the Dark Era and fought the Dark Creatures.
Pill Celestial Kevin Sage lived during the Ice Age, where he fought the Ice Demons.
Now, there is the Calamity King, whom he knew lived during the Calamity Era. He had no knowledge of that era yet, so he couldn’t tell if he was the Calamity King.
But since Paragon gave him a clue, he knew there must be some truth to it. Maybe he was the Calamity King who, in a way, had met the Calamity Dao.
If that were the case, then uncovering the secrets of the seven locks would be easy. But he would have to put a pin in that for now. He has a much more pressing matter to handle.
He turned away from the mural and decided to review Bello’s profile. After all, that was the main reason he came there.

chapters.title: Chapter 1435: Third Soul Warrior - Bello
paragraphs: After the issue with the mural was resolved, Kent turned his focus to Bello’s profile.
He is now a True Immortal with five strands of Immortal Qi. That was a huge leap from his initial cultivation before Kent killed him inside the Void Temple.
Now he had become a True Immortal.

However, while that is awesome, his focus shifted to his race, class, and, surprisingly, his bloodline. That was something new, something he never expected, considering Calix and Kenna do not have bloodlines yet.
However, he didn’t dwell much on that since he knew there was nothing bad about having a bloodline.
Looking at Bello’s appearance, he wasn’t too shocked when he saw his race. He is a [Soul Elf], a never-before-seen breed of Elves that specialize in the soul arts.
Of course, considering he is an archer, it is normal that he is an Elf. But unlike the ordinary breed of elves, he is intimately linked to the soul, which is a good thing.
Kent had already come to the conclusion that all his soul warriors would have their nature linked to the soul, so he was perfectly fine with that.
As for his class, it is a special one.
Class: Spirit Archer ↠ Description: With the soul as a conduit, the Spirit Archer is unstoppable. With souls on the battlefield, the Spirit Archer becomes unstoppable.
The class description is simple but contains so much. First was the soul as a conduit. Obviously, this one has to do with his connection to the soul.
As a soul warrior, he had no problem with that. He is connected to the soul on a much deeper level.
However, Bello is special.
Unlike Calix, who is a soul demon, and Kenna, whose affinity leans more toward the void, he is more rooted in the spirit.
This means his connection to the soul is much deeper than the rest. So his class, which is tied to the soul, allows him to link with the Soul Universe and do whatever he wants.

He can form arrows and all kinds of projectiles from the soul without much stress. Also, with these benefits, his stamina is much more preserved, since he is linked to the soul, so using it doesn’t put much strain on him.
The second half of the description had to do with soul spirits. Basically, the more he kills, or the more deaths there are on the battlefield, the more deadly he becomes.
He can form arrows and all kinds of weapons he can wield very easily. His class is versatile in matters of the soul and spirit. That alone shows just what kind of monster he is.
Bloodline: Grand Underworld Spirit Shaman ↠ Description: A messenger from the underworld with a mission to escort lost and stubborn spirits back into the River of Styx.
His bloodline is a strange one, but thanks to his affinities, a great deal of understanding was drawn from it.
Affinities: [Soul Affinity], [Spirit Affinity], [Underworld Essence Affinity]
The [Soul Affinity] is, of course, primary to all soul warriors, so it was normal to have it. However, the main chain lies with the [Spirit Affinity] and [Underworld Essence Affinity].

The Spirit Affinity allows him to interact with soul spirits. There is little to no information about how far he can take this affinity, but the mere fact that he can interact with them means he can do more than talk with them.
However, since there was no description of what he could do, Kent had to ask. Bello’s reply, however, left him in a state of shock.

It turned out he can do more than talk. To him, when someone dies, they become his subordinates. It doesn’t matter who, what, or when they were killed. As long as they are soul spirits, he has the power to command them.
Aside from that, he can temporarily possess a soul spirit and use their connection to their body to detonate their core.
So in this case, if a demigod were to die fresh in battle, Bello can possess their body, and even though they are dead, he can do one last thing, which is overloading and detonating their core.

That was all Kent needed to hear to know he had found the perfect warrior for when the odds are stacked against him. Although he can use the possession effect only once a day, if done correctly, he only needs to use it once to end the battle.
Aside from that, the [Underworld Essence Affinity] allows him a connection to an aspect of the underworld that Kent never expected.
His [Underworld Soul River] is linked directly to the River of Styx. So he was a bit puzzled when he learned that Bello could also harness the power of the River of Styx.
He can use it to form arrows and all kinds of weapons, provided he can wield them. That, in a way, makes him super deadly.
However, while he has three powerful affinities, he has only manifested two aspects and one innate ability.
Aspects: [Underworld Fisherman], [Spirit Eye]
These aspects were better explained by Bello. According to him, the [Underworld Fisherman] gives him some form of power to fish out lost souls and command them to fight for him.
It is random, so he can fish out a dud or a devil to do his deeds. Once a soul is caught, it remains tethered to his soul, making them his to command forever—unless, of course, they die.
As for the [Spirit Eye], he can see beyond the physical plane. His eyes let him see deep into the spirit plane, revealing what lies beyond the mortal realm.
Basically, he can see more than others can.
As for the innate ability, it is a bit special.
Innate Ability: [Underworld Escort]

This ability is rather insidious, regardless of how one tries to justify it. With the power to escort fallen souls, Bello can also drag living souls to the sea of the damned. He can open the door to the River of Styx, and with enough force, he can pull a soul inside.
Once they cross the gate, regardless of how healthy they are, they will drop dead.
Bello can see both the physical body and the spirit, so he can choose which to fight. This makes him very special and very deadly.
"I envy your innate ability, Bello. You are like the Grim Reaper walking among men."
Bello smiled.
He knew Kent was just joking, but hearing his words made him feel good. He extended his hand, and 12 Soul Crystals appeared.
"I used 2 for my bow, quiver, and armor."
"That is okay. If you need more, you can take them."
Bello nodded and took two more. Kent pocketed the rest. He already knew what to do with the rest.
"I will be heading to a dangerous place soon, so I want you to be on standby for when I call for help."
"I will be ready, Master."
Kent nodded.
Bello had already formed 5 Immortal Qi, so he is powerful enough to take on an Immortal King and even an Immortal Emperor.

Once he is done handling matters with the Midnight Shadows, he will figure the rest out as he goes. It is not that much of a struggle, considering he will be forming his second Flame Core before heading to Planet Brymrr.

chapters.title: Chapter 1436: Meeting An Old Friend Again
paragraphs: [Planet Bayla - Midnight Temple]

After leaving the Supreme Realm, Crimson Dagger and Thousand Blade made their way to the God Realm, where, after two days, they moved to the Immortal Realm. Then, after another three days, they headed to the High World.
When they arrived, Silent Requiem and Black Arrow were already back from the Void Seal and had made arrangements for the arrival of the Supreme Elder of the Midnight Shadows.
All Midnight Shadows that were not on an active mission had been recalled, and even a few immortals came to ensure this meeting would go on without any issues.
When they arrived, the first thing Thousand Blade asked for was where Kent was.
"Lord Faceless had already cleared the Void Forest and left. However, he has given us a way to contact him when you return with Lord Supreme."
"Then let’s call him," Thousand Blade said, and Black Arrow nodded.
He retrieved an item that looked like a jade stone, then crushed it.
Seated inside the Sword Tower, Kent opened his eyes and stood up. He had condensed a soul token when he left Planet Bayla the last time and gave it to Black Arrow, so when he crushed it, he felt it.
This was the call card he left them.
"Looks like they’ve returned," he muttered before teleporting into the Harem Tower to shower. It took him less than ten minutes to get that done.

Afterward, he went to check on Kaelith, who was still recovering. He hadn’t woken up just yet; however, since all his wounds had healed, he seemed to have recovered physically compared to before he was rescued.
Kent became happy seeing these improvements.
"Keep healing, buddy. We will have proper revenge when I ascend to the Immortal Realm." After saying that, he walked away and soon returned to Planet Bayla.

He appeared 20 km away from the Midnight Temple. Without even taking a step, he sensed a presence that had covered everywhere. The entire planet was covered by this presence, so he didn’t even bother to hide his own presence.
He advanced quickly toward the temple. In no time, he was standing at the entrance, where he could see lines of assassins, each clad in black armor, waiting for him.
This sight made him smile slightly. He was proud to see such a sight.
They were all powerful assassins, each with a name that would shake the hearts of many. He began walking toward the large throne standing majestically for him to sit on.

As he advanced toward it, he couldn’t help but wonder just how powerful his Midnight Shadows had become. He could sense no aura coming from any of them, as expected of assassins. It was as if they weren’t there.

If not that he could see them, there was just no way he could sense them, even if they had appeared inside his Soul Map. Perhaps if they were 100 meters away from him while his soul map is active, he could pick up on them.
But an assassin getting within 100 meters of a target is half the job done. So there was just no way he couldn’t be proud of them.
"I wonder how many of you are wearing your real faces," he muttered with a slight smile. They kept their faces calm, but deep down, they couldn’t help but smile.
The reason the midnight shadows are dangerous is their ability to change their faces and other aspects of their being.
Even if they aren’t Faceless Agents, Faceless left them with more than enough techniques to ensure every last one of them is protected.
Soon, Kent had made his way to the front, and that was when his eyes landed on Crimson Dagger. He let a smile appear on his face...
Crimson Dagger held a calm look on his face.
It can be said that he had known Faceless the longest. After all, he was the first assassin Faceless had recruited and personally trained. The two of them basically formed the midnight shadows.
They spent over a hundred years together before the second assassin was added. So if anything, he is the right person to confirm if Kent is indeed the Faceless Assassin.
Kent knew that, so he also prepared well before coming.
"You know, I never pegged you as someone who pays attention to their hair. When we met, you had low-cut hair and paid little to no attention to your appearance.
Now, it seems you have changed. I wonder which lady has finally managed to change you, Titus."
Crimson Dagger’s eyes narrowed for a second before they widened. However, he quickly calmed down and began a sentence...
"The black sheep is always..."
"Ready to be slaughtered by the butcher even if they had done nothing wrong."
"It is really you."
"In the flesh." Kent smiled and opened his arms wide. Although he is against hugging men, he made an exception for meeting an old friend.
Under the stunned looks on everyone’s faces, Crimson Dagger walked forward and gave his old friend and savior a big hug.
Everyone sighed, letting down their guard. They were all tense, for they had been informed someone important was coming to meet them, and so they came.
However, as assassins, they knew not to let their guard down, not when they had no idea who they were coming to meet.
Now that they could see what was happening, they knew even if Kent was a trouble, Crimson Dagger would handle him.
"You really have returned," Crimson Dagger said after making sure Kent was indeed a real person.
"I’ve indeed returned, buddy. It took some time, but I am back."
Crimson Dagger smiled, then turned to the hundreds of assassins present. "Everyone, greet the Faceless Assassin."
None of them hesitated. They all went down on their knees and gave a warrior’s bow. "Greetings to the Faceless Assassin."
Kent smiled and gestured for them to stand up. "Be on your feet, guys. I am back, but as you can see, I am as weak as they come, so there is no need to be overly modest."

Crimson Dagger smiled and shook his head. "Looks like you are still the same. Since when is the Faceless Assassin weak? When we met, I was an Immortal Lord, and you had just become a True Immortal, but when we dueled, I was defeated in just three moves."
Every last assassin present raised their brows, their gazes turning to Kent.
He smiled and responded, "That was because you were weak."
"Oh, do you want to have a go? I will even suppress myself to a Shadow King to level the playing field."
"Nope. I just had my bath, and I don’t intend to dirty my clothes with your green blood."

Chuckles and silent laughter filled the temple. Crimson Dagger just shook his head. He knew the real Faceless Assassin, so he could tell just how shameless he could be around people he considered family.
While he can be considered one of the most serious assassins to ever walk the face of the universe, when around people he is comfortable with, he can be the sweetest person.
Kent walked toward the throne and sat down. The familiar sensation he had always felt when he sat on this throne overwhelmed his senses.
The memory of the last meeting he had with his Midnight Shadows before he left for the Shadow Realm came to mind, making him take a deep sigh.
Looking at the hundreds of Shadows staring at him with respect, his pride as the founder of the Midnight Shadows slowly started to surface.
After taking in this feeling for a while, he started to address them.
"Thank you all for meeting me..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1437: Mission For The Midnight Shadows
paragraphs: Kent didn’t ask for the Midnight Shadows to meet him simply to tell them he is back. He came with a mission in mind, and now that he has their attention, he has decided to reveal the details.

"The reason I asked you here is to tell you all I am back. Yes, I am the Faceless Assassin, or at least I used to be. And yes, I am also Kent Madson—not that anyone will believe you if you tell them. But keep it a secret for your own safety.

I revealed my identity only to help you. One day, when you find yourself in trouble, there is a chance my name will come in handy. I happen to have some powerful friends out there," he smiled, and so did the Midnight Shadows.

Kent knew that in order to keep his Midnight Shadows safe, he had to make sure he had a handle on everything. If he were to hide who he is from them, they wouldn’t know who to go to if they couldn’t find their way back home.

Normally, they had been doing well while he was away. However, with the mission he had in mind, they would be entering uncharted territory, and with how his fame has spread, there is no doubt his name will carry both good and bad fortune.
He wants to make it a good fortune because once he ascends, the 13 lives he has lived will come into play. He will bring back his 13 legions and ensure that all under his command are protected.
So he wants his name to spread far and wide so that one day, when it is mentioned at the right place and at the right time, they will be helped.

Of course, there is also the issue of his belief that nobody would believe them. After all, he had no reputation as an assassin, so there is just no way anyone would believe them if some were to leak this information to the rest of the universe.
But even if they were to be believed, there is just no way anyone would focus more on that. After all, the Faceless Assassin was known as someone without a face.
If Kent is indeed such a person, then what is the guarantee that he is indeed the Faceless Assassin? What if the Faceless Assassin merely borrowed his face?
There are so many ways he can spin this, and it would make sense. However, after all that is said and done, the question still remains: why did Kent reveal such a big secret to the Midnight Shadows?

"I called you here because an enemy from the past is back, and she aims to take this universe by storm. What I am about to say is hidden knowledge from the Dark Era. In fact, not even the Universe Council knew this important detail."
Crimson Dagger furrowed his brow, hearing what Kent said. He lived and fought during the Dark Era, so he knew whatever Kent had to say was significant.
"During the Dark Era, when the Night Riders reigned supreme, there lived a race called Dark Creatures or Dark Fiends, depending on how you want to see it.
This race was the natural enemy of this universe, just like how the Void Beasts were enemies during the Primordial Era.

So, like what happens every Era, they breached this universe and attacked, aiming to kill and plunder. However, the brave warriors of this universe, led by the legendary Night Rider Captain Karl Duskbane, led the charge, and for years, a fierce battle raged.
In the end, we won after several great sacrifices." Kent paused and let the weight of his words settle in the air.

"However, I just found out we fought only half of the battle because back then our main enemy colluded with our own people and found a way to escape death. Now she is back, and she calls herself the Dark Queen."
"Impossible. The Dark Queen died. I witnessed it myself," Crimson Dagger said, his expression filled with confusion.
He was a True God then.
Unlike many who went into slumber to pass the Eras, he chose to remain conscious and, for Eras, fought many harrowing battles. This was his way of recruiting more shadows.
The day the Dark Queen died, he was injured and was being escorted away from the battlefield when the veiled lady put her sword through the Dark Queen’s heart.
He saw her die.

"On the contrary, my friend, the Dark Queen died twice. The one you witnessed was her sister, who assumed the role of the Queen of the Dark Creatures. She was killed by the second-in-command of the Night Riders.
However, her second death came at the hand of Karl Duskbane, the Captain of the Night Riders. But even that death was a means to an end.
Recently, my friends encountered a version of her, and she revealed she is back and has started her domination. Somehow, there are traitors in this universe who are aiding her.
So I am here today to remind you all why I formed the Midnight Shadows in the first place." They all became quiet, including Crimson Dagger.
The reason why he is feared even by Celestials is due to how much battle experience he has under his belt. He is the kind of assassin who has a million and one ways to kill his target.
However, even such a person is now quite simply because something he thought had long been handled is now back, and he just can’t wrap his mind around it.

"I created the Midnight Shadows so we can fight the battles in the shadows, away from the light. The threats that nobody sees coming are ours to handle, ensuring no harm comes to the innocent and defenseless.
So, while it will be dangerous, from today onward, our mission is to hunt down every possible version of the Dark Queen and eliminate her. This also extends to all who are aiding her.

They must all be eradicated silently and in the shadows. I am working on a way to locate her. Once that is done, the Midnight Shadows will start receiving missions at random. But for now, use the shadows, change your faces, and blend into the universe.
Use all you know to locate this dark threat and destroy it."
Every last Midnight Shadow responded to the mission. They had long ago decided to be part of something big.
Many were on a dark path, but after they were sworn into the ranks of the Midnight Shadows, their lives gained a sense of purpose, and that purpose had now revealed itself to them.
"I know it is a big mission, but I trust my shadows, and I know you will get the job done."

Crimson Dagger stood up and walked to the front. "Head back to your various outposts. The mission details will be posted soon. Once received, you must move out. The earlier we get started, the better."
They nodded, and soon every last one of them, including some of the Immortals, left. The only ones left were Adin, who is the leader of this Midnight Temple.
Black Arrow, Silent Requiem, and Thousand Blade also remained. Aside from them, Kent and Crimson Dagger were also there.
Kent had a mission for Thousand Blade, so he asked him to stay. Since he came with the other two, they decided to wait too.

sentences.text: Kent didn’t ask for the Midnight Shadows to meet him simply to tell them he is back.
He came with a mission in mind, and now that he has their attention, he has decided to reveal the details.
"The reason I asked you here is to tell you all I am back.
Yes, I am the Faceless Assassin, or at least I used to be.
And yes, I am also Kent Madson—not that anyone will believe you if you tell them.
But keep it a secret for your own safety.
I revealed my identity only to help you.
One day, when you find yourself in trouble, there is a chance my name will come in handy.
I happen to have some powerful friends out there," he smiled, and so did the Midnight Shadows.
Kent knew that in order to keep his Midnight Shadows safe, he had to make sure he had a handle on everything.
If he were to hide who he is from them, they wouldn’t know who to go to if they couldn’t find their way back home.
Normally, they had been doing well while he was away.
However, with the mission he had in mind, they would be entering uncharted territory, and with how his fame has spread, there is no doubt his name will carry both good and bad fortune.
He wants to make it a good fortune because once he ascends, the 13 lives he has lived will come into play.
He will bring back his 13 legions and ensure that all under his command are protected.
So he wants his name to spread far and wide so that one day, when it is mentioned at the right place and at the right time, they will be helped.
Of course, there is also the issue of his belief that nobody would believe them.
After all, he had no reputation as an assassin, so there is just no way anyone would believe them if some were to leak this information to the rest of the universe.
But even if they were to be believed, there is just no way anyone would focus more on that.
After all, the Faceless Assassin was known as someone without a face.
If Kent is indeed such a person, then what is the guarantee that he is indeed the Faceless Assassin?
What if the Faceless Assassin merely borrowed his face?
There are so many ways he can spin this, and it would make sense.
However, after all that is said and done, the question still remains: why did Kent reveal such a big secret to the Midnight Shadows?
"I called you here because an enemy from the past is back, and she aims to take this universe by storm.
What I am about to say is hidden knowledge from the Dark Era.
In fact, not even the Universe Council knew this important detail."

He lived and fought during the Dark Era, so he knew whatever Kent had to say was significant.
"During the Dark Era, when the Night Riders reigned supreme, there lived a race called Dark Creatures or Dark Fiends, depending on how you want to see it.
This race was the natural enemy of this universe, just like how the Void Beasts were enemies during the Primordial Era.
So, like what happens every Era, they breached this universe and attacked, aiming to kill and plunder.
However, the brave warriors of this universe, led by the legendary Night Rider Captain Karl Duskbane, led the charge, and for years, a fierce battle raged.
In the end, we won after several great sacrifices." Kent paused and let the weight of his words settle in the air.
"However, I just found out we fought only half of the battle because back then our main enemy colluded with our own people and found a way to escape death.
Now she is back, and she calls herself the Dark Queen."
"Impossible.
The Dark Queen died.
I witnessed it myself," Crimson Dagger said, his expression filled with confusion.
He was a True God then.
Unlike many who went into slumber to pass the Eras, he chose to remain conscious and, for Eras, fought many harrowing battles.
This was his way of recruiting more shadows.
The day the Dark Queen died, he was injured and was being escorted away from the battlefield when the veiled lady put her sword through the Dark Queen’s heart.
He saw her die.
"On the contrary, my friend, the Dark Queen died twice.
The one you witnessed was her sister, who assumed the role of the Queen of the Dark Creatures.
She was killed by the second-in-command of the Night Riders.
However, her second death came at the hand of Karl Duskbane, the Captain of the Night Riders.
But even that death was a means to an end.

chapters.title: Chapter 1438: Catching Up
paragraphs: "I will be needing your help in about 94 years from now," Kent said, turning toward Thousand Blade. He became stunned, but immediately recovered and asked.
"How can I be of help?" Although he had no idea what Kent wanted from him, the mere fact that the legendary Faceless Assassin asked for his help meant everything to him.
Being useful to the Faceless Assassin is a chance none of them will pass up on.

"I received an invite from the Dark Warden. He is organising a ball for the young talents in the Eastern Galaxy 94 years from now. Apparently, this ball is intended to foster unity among young talents preparing for the opening of the Chaos Rift.
I know he is inviting me with an ulterior motive, since I was the one who decimated his family on this planet.

Of course, it may also be a big misunderstanding, but because word will spread that I will attend that ball, there is a good chance some bad seeds will appear and try their luck at capturing or killing me.
So I need your protection from the shadows.
Find a way to get invited to the ball and keep a lookout for me. When things turn sideways, I will be counting on you to step in."
"I will do my best to handle this mission with absolute care," Thousand Blade said with a composed expression, showing he understood the assignment.
Inwardly, though, he is more than happy to show the Faceless Assassin what he is capable of.
"Though I have to ask, is Lord Faceless planning on also entering the Chaos Rift?"

"It sounded like a big deal, so of course I will enter. I will be embarking on a mission a year from today, so I can’t ascend to the Immortal Realm just yet. But in less than ten years, I will reach there and start preparing for whatever this Chaos Rift will bring."
Crimson Dagger smiled on the side. As someone who had known Kent the longest, he couldn’t help but have a sense of déjà vu.
For half the time he had known Faceless, if he wasn’t moving from one mission to another, he was exploring ancient ruins.
So, even long before Thousand Blade asked the question, he knew he had already made up his mind to enter the Chaos Rift.
"It is going to be the biggest adventure in the history of the Immortal Realm," Crimson Dagger said. "This Chaos Rift, from what I know, came from an entire Star System from the Chaos Era.
Rumour even has it that the rift will link to the Battleworld, where the last stand of the Chaos War took place—the same place the legendary Divine Beast Tamer fell alongside his Ten Calamity Beasts.
Trust me, this rift opening may be both good and bad, so you’d better prepare well. The last thing you want is walking into an unknown realm surrounded by millions of Immortal Lords and Demigods.
Many gods will even enter with avatars."

Kent nodded to his words. He had already made up his mind to enter the rift, so there was no need to start rethinking that decision now. If anything, hearing this place is linked to yet another life he had lived should be all the more reason to go there.
"I don’t do things without preparing first, buddy. When the time comes, I will be at my peak and ready to grab whatever opportunity the Chaos Era has for me."
After a few more discussions, the meeting with the Immortals ended, and they left. Soon, only Crimson Dagger remained.
"How are the others?" Kent asks.
Crimson Dagger was the first Midnight Shadow he had recruited. However, the day he made him a Faceless Agent, there were six others.
After he died, they became the Seven Elders of the Midnight Shadows.
"Broken Dagger is on a mission somewhere in the Supreme Realm. It has to do with the Silent Shadows. Over the years, they have resurfaced, but we are keeping them at bay for now.
Whispering Spear has been in seclusion for the past 4 million years after he became a Supreme. I am sure he had awakened something big, and so he had been working to comprehend it.

Needle Eye is now the Supreme Queen of the Dark Elven Race. The last I heard, she killed the original Supreme and stole her face. Personally, however, I think she is on a mission related to the Green Elves."
"Why do you assume that?" Kent asked.
"Six million years ago, rumours started spreading that the Supreme of the Green Elves found a dagger that used to belong to you.
And well, we both know how Needle Eye feels about you, so against my best judgment, I’m sure she is planning on getting it back."
"She was always a troublemaker, even long before I met her and made her a Midnight Shadow."
"Yes. She only grew more troublesome after you died." Crimson Dagger smiled and shook his head. "I wonder what she would do if she heard you are back."
"Better to keep it from her ears until she is done with her mission."
Crimson Dagger nodded and continued.
"Phantom Edge ventured into the Shadow Realm 8 million years ago. His life crystal is active, so I know for a fact he is still alive."
"He is always adventurous and fearless. When I met him, he was leading a ragtag group of ten wannabe assassins on a mission to kill a Warlord.

I warned him against it, but he was keen on it. When I found him, he had killed the Warlord but was also near death’s door." The image of a certain dark-haired, tan-skinned Pantherkin appeared in his mind.
"Phantom had always been reckless, but after you died, he did some amazing things. He even assassinated a General from the Soul Tower."
"Well then, he’d better return early, since I plan on bringing an end to the Soul Tower this time around."
Crimson Dagger seemed stunned, but he recovered, recognising the monster he was talking to.

"Dark Venom had joined the Venom Hall and has since climbed the ladder, becoming one of their top-ranking members. The last I heard, she had concocted her first Celestial Poison Pill and even earned the recognition of the Poison Dao."

Kent just smiled, already aware that the most dangerous assassin he had recruited into the ranks of the Midnight Shadows would never stop following the path of poison, regardless of how much time had passed.
Dark Venom was someone who had dedicated her entire life to walking the path of poison. If anything, he expected her to be ruling the Venom Hall by now.
"Lastly, the Black Widow vanished 2 million years ago. None of us knows where she has gone, but 300,000 years ago, I found one of her marks at the entrance of the Nameless Temple."
Kent widened his eyes. "You don’t think she actually entered that place."
"Knowing her, I wouldn’t put it past her. She had always done the impossible; entering a Calamity Zone seemed like something she would do.
Of course, there is a chance she left that there to throw me off. But as it stands right now, I don’t know where she is."
"What a headache." Kent thought for a moment, and then an idea popped into his mind. "Have you tried asking the Cult of Wisdom? Her second persona is linked to them, after all."

Crimson Dagger smirked. "Those arrogant nerds gave me nothing when I went to them. However, there was a rumour they had found a gem in a certain High World, so I don’t know if she had gone after him. She always likes smart people."
"Oh, a gem, they said?" A grin formed on Kent’s face.
