chapters.title: Chapter 1448: Raining Meteor
paragraphs: The only way Kent could break the spear the lion had unleashed was to sever its connection to it.
He thought of several ways, but when he measured his current strength against such a monster, he knew he was outmatched.
He could try outrunning the two beasts using the Jade Void Wings, but that would defeat the purpose of why he bothered facing them in the first place.
He was here to see how much he would fare against a powerful opponent. Although so far he had his ass handed to him, that doesn’t mean he had used all his trump cards.
In fact, he had yet to use any.
So with time running out, he knew he had to call one of his trump cards.
Kenna’s ability to sever connections to the soul was what he needed. So he called her, and thanks to that, he managed to destroy the spear.
Now, with Kenna having a soul battle with the lion, he was free to focus all his attention on the octopus.
"Try to keep up."
Saying that, all flame veins activated, and his dragon wings hummed with power. One half of the wings became green while the other turned red, each lit in flames.
They hardened, and with a gentle flap, he was upon the octopus. It tried to retaliate, but with Kent moving at that speed, all its tentacles were merely swinging wobbly in the air.

He was moving so fast that at some point, he started to believe he was the only one moving. However, that thought left his mind the next second when he saw the octopus stop and try to attack instead of focusing on countering his speed.
This made Kent slow down further.
However, the moment his speed came to a halt, he saw the sea turning to ice. From the ice, giant spears started to form.
Kent immediately realized he had to stop playing around and unleash the big guns.
"Let there be rain."
He flew up into the air, and when he was high enough, he activated 200 meteors. However, instead of making all 200 rain down at once, he focused only on one and caused it to move at a crashing speed.

The moment the octopus saw the large stone fall in its direction, a sense of dread filled its heart, so it also activated the ice shards, causing hundreds of them to shoot at both Kent and the stone falling toward it.
Kent activated the Chaos Scale Shields and started blocking the attacks. Meanwhile, the meteor was also being bombarded to the point that cracks appeared in it.
However, just when it shattered, a second one was in its place. Before long, the octopus was forced to defend against it.
But that was the start of its nightmare.
At the start of the battle, Kent wondered how he would be able to fight against such a monstrosity. He was but a bug compared to the monster.
However, now, watching as one meteor after another crashed down on the octopus, he could not help but feel like he was not as weak as he expected.

Sure, there were moments when even he would not have a chance to use any of these weapons. However, when the chance presented itself—like how this one did—there was just no way he would fail to use it.

He had formed 45,000 meteorites so far, and each week, more were added. So he could use them more if he had the chance to. But even if he could not use them as he expected, there were the 450 asteroids waiting for him to use.
Basically, he only needed the right conditions to use these weapons.
"Now that I think about it, instead of just creating attacking weapons, I need to think of ways to make weapons that can give me a better chance at using the attacking weapons."
Paragon had already told him that when it came to the soul universe, the only limitation was how deep his imagination was and how much soul essence he had.
Aside from these two, he could do just about anything.

So if his imagination was wild enough, there was a good chance he would be able to create something that would aid him in creating a good enough environment so he could use the meteorites and asteroids more effectively.
Provided the right conditions are met, with the power under his disposal, he could even kill an Immortal Lord.
"I will think about that later; for now, let’s make sure this beast dies fast enough so I can be on my way."
More and more attacks managed to land on the beast, but some were defended against. In the end, after the 200th meteorite landed on its body, it was sent crashing into the sea.
The entire water was soaked red, showing just how many injuries it had sustained.
But because it was still breathing and healing thanks to the water, Kent decided to unleash another trump card.
The sky turned red and green just as the tip of a finger appeared through the clouds.
He decided to see how powerful the finger of destruction had become.
The octopus felt the danger as the Finger of Destruction appeared, so it tried to make a run for it. However, the power of the technique prevented it from even moving an inch.
So it could only try to defend itself as the finger moved toward it. In the end, against all odds, the octopus could not handle the Finger of Destruction, and so the battle came to an end.
Its humongous body sank to the bottom of the sea, which Kent did not chase after. It had already died, judging by how fatal the Finger of Destruction was.
Half of its body was reduced to nothing. That alone was enough proof that he had won and that the octopus was dead for good.
However, he had some concerns about the Finger of Destruction.
"While it has now become powerful after forming the second Flame Core, even with both working hand in hand, I was only able to unleash 45% of its true power.
Just what am I missing here? I have the energy to sustain and use it at least 10 times before running out. So how come I could only use 45% of it?"
This question left him disappointed. However, feeling the pain coming from parts of his body where he had sustained injuries, he knew he had to deal with that first.
He won, but that was because he used the meteors.

While that was part of his strength, if he had not gotten the chance to use them, he would have been forced to flee. But he won, and that was enough evidence that he had grown much stronger than he thought.
"I hope when this journey is over, I will be able to develop more weapons to better aid me in combat."
Just as he said that, a powerful howl came from under the ocean. A few seconds later, Kenna burst from the water, holding a reddish orb about the size of three basketballs in both hands.
The smile on her face told Kent she was very happy, so he did not bother to ask her the questions he wanted to.
"Go back and start absorbing it. Next time, I will call Calix or Bello."
She frowned; however, what Kent said next made her smile again.
"There are many battles ahead of us, so the earlier you absorb it, the better."
"Then I will be leaving. See you later." She vanished back into the soul universe, where she immediately started absorbing the soul orb she had extracted directly from the lion’s soul.

Kent, however, used the Soul Map to scan the lion’s body. Considering it death came at the hand of a soul attack, it was perfectly intact. After a few moments of thought, he stored it in the tower storage and resumed his journey.

He was but a bug compared to the monster.
However, now, watching as one meteor after another crashed down on the octopus, he could not help but feel like he was not as weak as he expected.
Sure, there were moments when even he would not have a chance to use any of these weapons.
However, when the chance presented itself—like how this one did—there was just no way he would fail to use it.
He had formed 45,000 meteorites so far, and each week, more were added.
So he could use them more if he had the chance to.
But even if he could not use them as he expected, there were the 450 asteroids waiting for him to use.
Basically, he only needed the right conditions to use these weapons.
"Now that I think about it, instead of just creating attacking weapons, I need to think of ways to make weapons that can give me a better chance at using the attacking weapons."
Paragon had already told him that when it came to the soul universe, the only limitation was how deep his imagination was and how much soul essence he had.
Aside from these two, he could do just about anything.

So if his imagination was wild enough, there was a good chance he would be able to create something that would aid him in creating a good enough environment so he could use the meteorites and asteroids more effectively.
Provided the right conditions are met, with the power under his disposal, he could even kill an Immortal Lord.
"I will think about that later; for now, let’s make sure this beast dies fast enough so I can be on my way."
More and more attacks managed to land on the beast, but some were defended against.
In the end, after the 200th meteorite landed on its body, it was sent crashing into the sea.
The entire water was soaked red, showing just how many injuries it had sustained.
But because it was still breathing and healing thanks to the water, Kent decided to unleash another trump card.
The sky turned red and green just as the tip of a finger appeared through the clouds.
He decided to see how powerful the finger of destruction had become.
The octopus felt the danger as the Finger of Destruction appeared, so it tried to make a run for it.
However, the power of the technique prevented it from even moving an inch.
So it could only try to defend itself as the finger moved toward it.
In the end, against all odds, the octopus could not handle the Finger of Destruction, and so the battle came to an end.
Its humongous body sank to the bottom of the sea, which Kent did not chase after.
It had already died, judging by how fatal the Finger of Destruction was.
Half of its body was reduced to nothing.
That alone was enough proof that he had won and that the octopus was dead for good.
However, he had some concerns about the Finger of Destruction.
"While it has now become powerful after forming the second Flame Core, even with both working hand in hand, I was only able to unleash 45% of its true power.
Just what am I missing here?
I have the energy to sustain and use it at least 10 times before running out.
So how come I could only use 45% of it?"
This question left him disappointed.
However, feeling the pain coming from parts of his body where he had sustained injuries, he knew he had to deal with that first.
He won, but that was because he used the meteors.
While that was part of his strength, if he had not gotten the chance to use them, he would have been forced to flee.
But he won, and that was enough evidence that he had grown much stronger than he thought.
"I hope when this journey is over, I will be able to develop more weapons to better aid me in combat."
Just as he said that, a powerful howl came from under the ocean.
A few seconds later, Kenna burst from the water, holding a reddish orb about the size of three basketballs in both hands.
The smile on her face told Kent she was very happy, so he did not bother to ask her the questions he wanted to.
"Go back and start absorbing it.
Next time, I will call Calix or Bello."
She frowned; however, what Kent said next made her smile again.
"There are many battles ahead of us, so the earlier you absorb it, the better."
"Then I will be leaving.
See you later." She vanished back into the soul universe, where she immediately started absorbing the soul orb she had extracted directly from the lion’s soul.
Kent, however, used the Soul Map to scan the lion’s body.
Considering it death came at the hand of a soul attack, it was perfectly intact.
After a few moments of thought, he stored it in the tower storage and resumed his journey.

chapters.title: Chapter 1449: Sword Intent Awakening
paragraphs: [Dream Continent - Dream City - Planet Brymrr]
There are seven extremely large continents on Planet Brymrr.
One of them is the Dream Continent. It is home to the Elves and is also the most beautiful and powerful continent in the world.
Of course, not only do Elves live there, but they also rule it despite there being other races, some even more powerful than most Elves living there.
All of the planet’s alchemy comes from there, since the Elves, long before this planet became a unique planet, had cemented their status as the Alchemy Central of the entire world.
They have a legendary alchemist who, over the years, has done nothing but ensure the world of Alchemy was never dull.
This alchemy leader is a recently ascended Supreme who, long before she reached that stage, could concoct Pseudo-Supreme Pills.
When she finally reached the supreme stage, she announced to the entire world that she would host a live demonstration in 6 months. At this event, she would attempt her first Supreme Pill Concoction.
This is her way of finally reaching the rank of a Pill Supreme.

Legend has it that a very long time ago, she received enlightenment from the Pill Dao, and in that enlightenment, she was given a pill recipe that, to this day, the universe of Alchemy has been looking for.
Dao Enlightenment Pill
It is a pill said to directly connect one to the Dao they practice when consumed. This means if Kent were to take it, there is a big chance he would be connected to the Sword and Pill Dao.

Of course, one would not come face-to-face with the Dao. However, getting a glimpse of the Dao, even from several billion light-years away, can transform just anyone from mediocrity to legendary status.
It is the pill of a lifetime, and since it was given to her by the Pill Dao, it cannot be stolen nor pressured to use it. She had to concoct it at her own pace and time.
This was why two months ago, just when Pseudo-Pill Supreme Ainna was preparing to make a simple pill, the most unexpected person appeared at her doorstep.
She knew powerful people would come to her in the hope of getting their hands on the first-ever Dao Enlightenment Pill.
However, she was taken aback when this person appeared at her doorstep.
At first, seeing her again made her frown and bitter. However, she became happy a few moments later when this friend of hers told her something unexpected.
It turned out that a very long time ago, the two of them met and made plans to reach the peak together, one as a swordswoman and the other an alchemist.
That promise became a betrayal when one of them ran off with a boy who later broke her heart and left her stuck at the god stage for countless years now.
She hated her for that betrayal, but seeing her friend Inaya back, she had no choice but to forgive her. After all, being mad at the ruler of the entire planet isn’t something she wanted.
So they have been living together since then, sharing stories of things that happened while she was away.
After learning all she needed to, Inaya decided to rest and wait for the event that Ainna announced would be happening in 6 months.
She knew she would be the recipient of the Dao Enlightenment Pill, but to make others happy, she let Ainna entertain them, even allowing her to take their gifts with a smile on her beautiful face.
Of course, she expected her days to be as smooth as ever, especially after she learned someone new had appeared on the Sword Dao tablet.
She knew for a fact that Jest had reincarnated because, in her heart, there is only one man who could impress the Sword Dao, and that person is Jest.
But that was ruined when news suddenly began spreading that the Sword Intent left behind by Lord Genesis several years ago had awakened.
One of the reasons why she came back to the Dream Continent was so she could be close to something that used to belong to Lord Genesis.

It was said that before he died, he managed to glimpse into the realm above the Sword Celestial stage. That small glimpse was enough for him to improve his sword intent to the point he was able to leave a part of it, which, since he was gone, had helped countless swordsmen gain enlightenment.
It was even said that the reason why Planet Brymrr still stood after countless wars plagued the universe was because of that sword intent.
So, for such an item to awaken all of a sudden after sleeping for billions of years and through many generations, she couldn’t help but come to a sudden conclusion.
"He is here."
"Who is here?" Ainna asked, staring at Inaya, whose gaze pierced into the vastness of space, staring at the awakened sword intent.
Before today, it was disguised as a brown sword. However, now it seems to have transformed into a bald child about 13 years old.
"Jest. He is back... and I think he is on this planet."
"You always say that ever since that Kent Madson person’s name appeared on the Sword Dao Tablet. When are you going to stop obsessing over him and just move on?
For heaven’s sake, that bastard abandoned you when you needed him the most, so even if he is back, so what?" Ainna shot Inaya a fierce glance.

"Or have you forgotten it took me 100,000 years to transform you from a mess back into a living person. I don’t have the energy or time to do that again. So you’d better put your shit together and get over him."
Inaya sighed, her expression softening. "As if that is an easy thing to do. He is my heart demon, Ainna. I tried many times to move on, but he always comes back to haunt me.

Or do you think I went into a slumber for billions of years because I love to sleep? I tried many times to move on, but until he returned from the dead and made up for what he had promised me, the only thing I could do was obsess over him."
Ainna smirked, but seeing her friend, who was usually fierce like a tiger, now appear soft and emotional, her hatred died down a bit. But she still made her feelings known.
"If that bastard is indeed back like you said, then he’d better pray I don’t find him first. Because if I do, he is going to wish he had never hurt you."
Inaya smiled. "All the more reason for me to protect him from you. The last thing I want is him ending up dead again before I can get back at him myself."

"Tsk, keep defending him." Ainna paused and gave her next words a critical examination before saying them. "Just so you know, that bitch he ditched you for has become a Celestial millions of years ago, while you are still stuck at the Universal God stage with a heart demon."
Inaya shot her friend a sidelong glance before a sigh escaped her lips. "Don’t worry. I will kill her one day, after I kill that bastard."
"As if I will believe that."
They became silent, thinking about what all this means. Now that the sword intent had awakened, many powerful swordsmen would soon appear, so they had to prepare.
Who knows what kind of battle will soon break out?
Most importantly, who knows why it had awakened after being dormant for so long.
Meanwhile, back in the unknown forest, Kent was only a few thousand miles from reaching the edge of teh forest, where he would begin his final journey through its harrowing depths.
He had no idea where he would end up after crossing the forest, but he knew he had to be careful since, even long before he reached it, he could sense an ominous presence coming from within.
Just when he was a few hundred meters away, he came to a stop and scanned his surroundings. Finding no immediate danger, he landed and quickly made his way to a small clearing right atop a mountain.
He wanted to let the Tower do its thing before he made a decision.
The last thing he wanted was to walk into an unknown trap.
He might be powerful for someone of his rank, but if he were to walk into the den of an Immortal Lord, he would die for sure.

chapters.title: Chapter 1450: Plan to Cross The Unknown Forest
paragraphs: Kent settled down on the mountain peak, and while he waited for the Tower to finish its scan, he also started using the soul map to scan the 80,000 km radius around him.
Although he had also concluded that, against a powerful opponent, his soul map is flawed, he had been working actively to fix that issue.
He observed that if the target is much stronger than him, they only register inside the soul map when they are a few meters away.
However, if he were to flood the soul map radius with soul essence, then even from a 30,000 km radius, he would be able to see them.
But that is not good for him.
He knew he would be facing powerful foes at every turn on this journey, so he had to find a way to be able to see his targets long before they spot him.
An average True Immortal can easily sense anything within a 100,000 km radius.
However, not many have that much time and energy to spread their senses that vast. So most of the time, he wouldn’t have to worry about his opponent sensing him before he did.
Of course, he wouldn’t be betting on that, especially when the location he may find himself is a no-man’s land. Where there is danger, everyone tends to be on high alert.

However, even after spending about 30 minutes trying to make sense of how to be ahead of his opponents, he came out empty-handed. It turned out there was only so much he could do by pumping so much soul essence into the soul map.
"If I want to sense more, I must increase my soul cultivation. That is the only way." He sighed, not out of frustration but just plain disappointment.
If he can’t see that far, even though his senses have covered it, then he most certainly would only have to wait until he becomes a Tier 20 soul cultivator and even higher.
But would his opponents wait till he is Tier 20 before sneaking up on him?
"Such a shame. If I could concoct a Tier 15 Soul Ascension Pill, while that won’t help me break through to Tier 20, it would strengthen it even more. Maybe that would allow me to sense more."
His mastery in alchemy is only at Tier 13, so he could only hope for now.
"But I can go ahead and make it so that if I can’t sense them, they also can’t sense me either." This sounded like a good and achievable idea, so he decided to give it a try.
However, he had only begun brainstorming when the Tower prompted him that she had finished her scan.
"Tell me what you have discovered, Tower."
[There is good and bad news.]
"Good news first..." he didn’t even hesitate.
[The good news is that the moment you cross this forest, you will appear on a main road. That road leads to a city, judging by the tracks left by what appear to be carriages.
However, the bad news is that this forest has four sections, each ruled by an Immortal Lord or at least appears to be.
We are currently in the Eastern section, ruled by the Blade-Winged Falcon. She is one of the fastest beasts in this forest.
Even more bad news: we are currently in the territory of an Immortal Monarch Mountain Goat who has already sensed your presence and is sneaking up on you.]
ROAR
A powerful roar, almost like that of a dragon, filled the air.
"Goats don’t roar, do they?" Kent asked just as his sword appeared in his grip. Then with a powerful swing, he struck back, meeting the metallic hooves of a 30-meter-tall goat.
The impact rattled his arm, pushing him back a few meters. The goat landed on the mountain, its nostrils oozing smoke. Its gaze locked on Kent, and with every exhale, the danger tightened around him.
"What are you doing in my territory, human?"
"Oh, you can speak." Kent was taken aback, but he didn’t dwell on it. He knew his life was in danger yet again.
However, the allure of locking in battle with this goat seems to be getting the best of him. Just looking at the goat seems to bring back old memories.
Back when Jest was exploring the Sword Valley, looking for a way to ascend to the Immortal World, he came close to being killed by a Mountain Goat.
It was one of the most dangerous battles he had fought before ascending to the immortal realm. So seeing one again was like being back in the Sword Valley.
However, he had no plans of dying today, not when he had just learned there is an Immortal Lord-level beast inside the forest and that it may have already sensed his presence.
"I am just passing through, Uncle Goat," he said, keeping his grip firm on his sword. At any change in the goat’s posture, he would attack.
Of course, there was just no way he would spend a second fighting a senseless battle. If there is a chance, he would make a fast exit.
"My queen had already sensed your battle with the octopus and the lion and sent me to fetch you. You can either come with me willingly, or I will drag your unconscious body there if I have to."
"What does she want with me?" Kent asked.
He had already prepared an escape route, so depending on Uncle Goat’s answer, he would pull a fast one.
However, while he was prepared to make a run for it, a part of him kept telling him to go with the goat. If there is one thing he knows and trusts about his sixth sense, it is to always trust it.
If it says going with the Goat is the best option for him, then he will.
So he took a deep breath and asked the same question again, "What does she want with me?"
"You killed two of her people, so you must answer for that. Now, do you want to come peacefully or forcefully?"
"Hmm," Kent hummed, then he nodded.
"Lead the way."
Running was the only option he had.

However, if he were caught, he knew he would be in trouble. He might have the Jade Void Wings, but he knew for a fact that, against an Immortal Lord who specialises in speed, there is no way he could outrun her.
So hearing what she had to say seemed logical. After all, she came in peace, even sending a goat to fetch him.
’I really should improve my sensing abilities, or else one day I might end up dead without even knowing how.’
They took flight and soon headed deeper into the forest. Along the way, Kent couldn’t help but dread the fact that he had actually thought of running.
The sheer number of Immortal-level beasts they kept passing by was just too staggering. He never expected there to be this many beasts.
With just a single command, thousands would surround him before he could even take ten steps.
’If there is a tour guide here, now is the time they would say, "Welcome to the world of immortals."’
Kent couldn’t help but let out a small chuckle. A couple of minutes later, a rather lavish building, one built from wood, came into sight.

Kent narrowed his eyes at it, a wave of dread filling his heart as they neared it. Inside, he could sense a terror looking directly at him. It was as if her mere gaze was enough to burn a hole in his heart.
’There goes my plan to cross the unknown forest,’ Kent smiled inwardly. A few seconds later, they landed before the wooden house.
"My queen, I brought the human," the goat said, transforming into a demihuman so he could kneel.
"Enter, human."
The door swung open, and Kent stepped in. It closed behind him.
"So you are the one who killed two of my people."

"Lead the way."
Running was the only option he had.
However, if he were caught, he knew he would be in trouble.
He might have the Jade Void Wings, but he knew for a fact that, against an Immortal Lord who specialises in speed, there is no way he could outrun her.
So hearing what she had to say seemed logical.
After all, she came in peace, even sending a goat to fetch him.
’I really should improve my sensing abilities, or else one day I might end up dead without even knowing how.’
They took flight and soon headed deeper into the forest.
Along the way, Kent couldn’t help but dread the fact that he had actually thought of running.
The sheer number of Immortal-level beasts they kept passing by was just too staggering.
He never expected there to be this many beasts.
With just a single command, thousands would surround him before he could even take ten steps.
’If there is a tour guide here, now is the time they would say, "Welcome to the world of immortals."’
Kent couldn’t help but let out a small chuckle.
A couple of minutes later, a rather lavish building, one built from wood, came into sight.
Kent narrowed his eyes at it, a wave of dread filling his heart as they neared it.
Inside, he could sense a terror looking directly at him.
It was as if her mere gaze was enough to burn a hole in his heart.
’There goes my plan to cross the unknown forest,’ Kent smiled inwardly.
A few seconds later, they landed before the wooden house.
"My queen, I brought the human," the goat said, transforming into a demihuman so he could kneel.
"Enter, human."
The door swung open, and Kent stepped in.
It closed behind him.
"So you are the one who killed two of my people."
